claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital for 11 weeks (within 12-week limit)
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question for our assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you, I need to know about your child or children. Let me start with the basics:

**What is your child's age?** (or if you have multiple children, please tell me about each one)

The Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age, so this is the first important factor. Please let me know:
- How old is the child (or children)?
- What are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I've got one child - Alex, who's 8 years old. They live here at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's really helpful. So we're looking at **Alex, who is 8 years old** - that means Alex falls into the under 16 category, which is good news as this is generally the most straightforward category for Child Benefit eligibility.

Let me continue with the next checks we need to go through.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, I'd expect this to be a straightforward "yes", but I need to confirm this to be thorough.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh yes, Alex isn't working at all - they're only 8, so they're just in school at the moment!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. So Alex is at school and not in any paid work. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

For an 8-year-old at school, this would typically be "yes", but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't get any benefits in their own name. It's just me as the parent who might claim things.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I'd expect. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 8 years old and in school, I'd expect the answer to be no, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - Alex is way too young for an apprenticeship! They're just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely! That makes sense - Alex is definitely too young for an apprenticeship. Let me continue to the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now we're at an important check - **residency requirements**. Child Benefit has specific residency rules for the claimant (that's you).

Let me ask: **Do you normally live in the UK?** 

This is the main route for most people. However, there are also other ways you might qualify if you don't normally live in the UK - for example, if you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, pre-settled status with certain conditions, or if you're a Crown servant living abroad.

For now, let me start with the main question: Are you normally resident in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK normally. I'm based here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's great. So you normally live in the UK, which means you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to check responsibility for Alex. The question is:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned earlier that Alex lives at home with you, so I'd expect this to be straightforward. But to be clear, responsibility means either:
- You live with the child, OR
- You contribute to their upkeep (like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.)

Since Alex lives with you at home, you clearly meet this requirement. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives here with me at home, so I'm responsible for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - you live with Alex and are responsible for them. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check something important:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else told you they're planning to claim for Alex?**

In most cases, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. If there's a situation where multiple people might be claiming, we need to know about it. But based on what you've told me so far, I'd expect the answer to be no. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check on Alex's living situation:

**Where does Alex normally live? Specifically:**
- Is Alex in hospital?
- Is Alex in local authority care?
- Is Alex fostered?
- Or is Alex living at home with you in a normal family arrangement?

Based on what you've said so far, I'd expect Alex is living at home with you normally, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex has been in hospital for a while now - about a couple of months or so. It's been quite a difficult time for us.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital - that sounds like a difficult time for your family. Thank you for sharing that information.

Since Alex is in hospital, I need to check on the specific duration of the hospital stay, as this affects Child Benefit eligibility. Let me get the details on the hospital rules.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you - that's helpful information. I can see that hospital stays have specific rules.

**How long exactly has Alex been in hospital?** You mentioned about a couple of months - I need to know if it's been more or less than **12 weeks (about 3 months)**, as this is the key threshold for Child Benefit eligibility when a child is in hospital.

Can you give me a more precise timeframe?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been 11 weeks now. So just under the 3 months.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex has been in hospital for **11 weeks**, which is just under the 12-week limit. That's important information.

Let me navigate to the hospital duration check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I have the hospital duration check. Since Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, which is under the 12-week limit, we need to check one more thing:

**Before Alex was admitted to hospital this time, has Alex been in hospital or residential accommodation within the last 28 days prior to this current stay?**

This is important because of the "linking rule" - if there was a hospital stay within 28 days before this one, the time counts together cumulatively. For example, if Alex had been in hospital for 2 weeks, came home for 20 days, and then went back in for 11 weeks, the total would be 13 weeks (which would exceed the limit).

So the question is: has Alex had any previous hospital stays that would link to this current one?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, this is the first time Alex has been in hospital like this. There haven't been any other hospital stays recently before this one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good to know - so this is Alex's first hospital admission and there are no previous stays to link to. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now there's one more important check for children in hospital:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while they're in hospital?**

This could include things like:
- Visiting expenses (travel, parking, accommodation)
- Buying Alex items like clothes, books, games, toiletries
- Paying for phone calls or other support
- Any other regular contributions towards Alex's needs while in hospital

The key word is "regularly" - it needs to be ongoing spending, not just occasional visits. Does this apply to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I still buy things for Alex - clothes, magazines, their favorite snacks and food. I try to keep things as normal as possible for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's wonderful that you're supporting Alex like that - it clearly shows your commitment to their wellbeing during this difficult time. The regular spending on clothes, magazines, snacks, and food absolutely counts as regularly spending money on Alex while in hospital.

Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost there. The final check is:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while in hospital?**

In other words - are you covering Alex's costs (or are they covered through the NHS hospital), or is the local council paying for Alex's care and accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying for anything. It's all through the NHS - it's a hospital stay for medical treatment, not something the council is involved with.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's clear - the NHS is covering the hospital treatment, and the local council isn't involved in paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance. This means you meet this final requirement.

Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

Congratulations! Based on the information you've provided, you qualify for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**Child:** Alex (age 8)

**Key factors that make you eligible:**
1. ✅ Alex is under 16 years old
2. ✅ You normally live in the UK
3. ✅ You are responsible for Alex and live with them
4. ✅ You are the only person claiming for Alex
5. ✅ Alex is not working or in disqualifying work
6. ✅ The hospital stay is 11 weeks (under the 12-week limit)
7. ✅ You are regularly spending money on Alex while in hospital (clothes, magazines, snacks, food)
8. ✅ The local council is not paying for Alex's care

### Important Points:

**Hospital Stay Rule:** Child Benefit will continue while Alex is in hospital **as long as:**
- The cumulative hospital stay doesn't exceed 12 weeks total
- You continue to regularly spend money on Alex
- The local council isn't paying for care

You're currently at 11 weeks, so you have approximately 1 more week before reaching the 12-week limit. If Alex needs to stay longer, it would affect your eligibility unless exceptional circumstances apply.

### What to Do Next:

1. **Apply for Child Benefit** if you haven't already done so through HMRC at www.gov.uk/child-benefit
2. **Keep records** of your regular spending on Alex while in hospital (receipts, etc.)
3. **Report any changes** to HMRC, especially if Alex's hospital stay extends beyond 12 weeks or if the local council becomes involved in funding
4. **Stay in touch with HMRC** about Alex's medical situation

I hope Alex makes a good recovery soon. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old (under 16, automatic qualification). Alex is not working or in paid employment (meets work requirement). Alex is not receiving any benefits in their own right (meets benefit requirement). Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship (meets apprenticeship requirement). You normally live in the UK (meets residency requirement). You live with Alex and are responsible for their care (meets responsibility requirement). No other person is claiming Child Benefit for Alex (meets single claimant requirement). Although Alex is currently in hospital, the cumulative hospital stay is 11 weeks, which is under the 12-week limit. Importantly, you are regularly spending money on Alex while in hospital (buying clothes, magazines, snacks, and food), which is an exception to the 12-week rule. The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance (the NHS is covering the hospital treatment). All eligibility requirements are met.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Although Alex is currently in hospital, you meet all the eligibility criteria because: (1) Alex is under 16 years old; (2) you are normally resident in the UK; (3) you are responsible for Alex and live with them; (4) you are the only person claiming for Alex; (5) the hospital stay is under 12 weeks; (6) you are regularly spending money on Alex while in hospital; and (7) the local council is not paying for Alex's care. Child Benefit will continue while Alex is in hospital as long as you maintain regular spending on them and the cumulative hospital stay does not exceed 12 weeks (currently at 11 weeks)."
